issues.legal_issue: Long and immemorial use of one part of an extensive property does not, without proof connecting the disputed part to that use, establish that the disputed part has become wakf property.
material_facts: The plaintiffs and their ancestors had long held and managed the extensive property, and no dedication by declaration of intention or by will was pleaded or proved.
Muslims had been allowed to offer prayers in a mosque on part of the property for at least 25 years, and that mosque was found to be wakf property.
The disputed portion was where the defendants placed a Tazia; the defendants produced no satisfactory proof that this portion had been dedicated as wakf.
The claim before the Court concerned the disputed portion, not the status of the entire property.
issues.conclusion: The defendants did not establish that the disputed portion had become wakf property. The appeal was dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: Where prior ownership and management are established and no express dedication by declaration or will is proved, the party asserting that the property later became wakf through long and immemorial user must establish that claim. Proof that a mosque on one part of an extensive property was used for prayer may establish wakf status for the mosque, but does not establish that the entire property, or a distinct disputed portion, is wakf. The judgment cites no statutory provision or earlier case.

rule.if: civil_appeal_on_wakf_claim and prior_owner_management_shown and no_express_dedication_proved and mosque_use_limited_to_part and no_proof_of_disputed_plot_dedication

predicates.civil_appeal_on_wakf_claim: The proceeding is a civil appeal concerning whether a disputed part of property is wakf.
predicates.prior_owner_management_shown: The claimant and predecessors had long held and managed the property.
predicates.no_express_dedication_proved: No dedication by declaration of intention or by will was pleaded or proved.
predicates.mosque_use_limited_to_part: People used a mosque for prayer on one part of the larger property.
predicates.no_proof_of_disputed_plot_dedication: The party asserting wakf status produced no satisfactory evidence connecting the disputed part to a dedication or religious use.

issues.definition: When a civil appeal concerns a wakf claim, prior ownership and management are shown, no express dedication is proved, and mosque use is confined to another part without evidence connecting the disputed plot to a dedication, the disputed plot is not established as wakf.
